intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

selected_hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina district, Marrakech Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the heart of Marrakech by wandering through the UNESCO-listed Djemaa el-Fna square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians by day, then witness the square transform into a massive open-air food market at dusk. Explore the labyrinthine souks of the old medina for spices, leather goods, and handcrafted treasures.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp
experiences.description: Ride a camel into the golden Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset and spend the night in a traditional Berber desert camp. Enjoy a campfire dinner with tagine and mint tea, listen to Gnawa music under a sky blazing with stars, and wake up early to watch the sunrise paint the dunes in shades of orange and red.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Step back into Morocco's imperial past with a self-guided or local-guided tour of the stunning 19th-century Bahia Palace, adorned with intricate zellige tilework and carved cedarwood ceilings. Then visit the nearby Saadian Tombs, a hidden necropolis of the Saadian dynasty featuring beautifully decorated mausoleums rediscovered in 1917.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in a riad kitchen and learn to prepare authentic Moroccan dishes such as chicken bastilla, lamb tagine with preserved lemons, and homemade harira soup. Begin with a guided tour of the spice souks to source fresh ingredients, then enjoy your feast with fellow travelers over mint tea and msemen flatbread.

experiences.name: Todra Gorge Rock Climbing & Hike
experiences.description: Adventure through the dramatic Todra Gorge, where towering 300-meter limestone canyon walls rise from a crystal-clear river. Hike along the gorge floor, scramble up beginner-friendly rock faces with a local guide, and explore traditional Berber villages clinging to the canyon edges. A thrilling stop on the route between Marrakech and the Sahara.
experiences.location: Todra Gorge, Tinghir Province, High Atlas foothills

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina district, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and transit from Marrakech Menara Airport to your riad in the Medina. Take a petit taxi (negotiate to ~60-80 MAD) or shared bus (Bus 19, ~4 MAD) to Djemaa el-Fna.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique stay in Djemaa el-Fna. After freshening up, take a gentle orientation walk through the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square. Observe the snake charmers, henna artists, and street performers. Stroll into the nearby souks (Souk Semmarine) to get your bearings — no pressure to buy on day one.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Djemaa el-Fna as the square transforms into a massive open-air night market. Browse the food stalls (numbered 1–100+) — try harira soup (5 MAD), merguez sandwiches (15 MAD), and fresh-squeezed orange juice (4 MAD). Watch the storytellers and musicians as the square comes alive.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Pick up a msemen (Moroccan flatbread) with honey and argan oil from a street vendor near Djemaa el-Fna (~10-15 MAD)
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna night food stalls — harira soup, kefta brochettes, and fresh OJ for under 50 MAD total

day_by_day.notes: Keep your valuables secure in the square — use a money belt. Exchange some cash at the airport or a bureau de change in the Medina (avoid hotel exchange rates). Budget tip: a full dinner at the square stalls costs 40-60 MAD (~$4-6 USD).

day_by_day.morning: Early rise for a traditional Moroccan breakfast at a local café near the riad — mint tea, msemen, amlou (almond-argan dip), and hard-boiled eggs (~20-30 MAD). Then visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (free exterior viewing — non-Muslims cannot enter). Walk to the Ben Youssef Madrasa, one of the most stunning Islamic schools in North Africa (entry ~70 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Musée de Marrakech housed in a 19th-century palace (~50 MAD entry). Afterwards, lose yourself in the labyrinthine souks — Souk des Teinturiers (dyers' souk), Souk Cherratin (leather), and Souk des Bijoutiers (jewellery). Practice your bargaining skills — always start at 30-40% of the asking price.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD) just before closing, then walk through the Kasbah neighbourhood. For dinner, head to Rue Bab Agnaou for local restaurants serving traditional tagine and couscous. End the evening with a stroll through the lit-up Djemaa el-Fna.

meals.breakfast: Local café near the riad — mint tea, msemen, amlou (~25 MAD)
meals.lunch: Sandwich shop in the souks — kefta or chicken sandwich with harissa (~15-20 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant near Kasbah — lamb tagine with bread and mint tea (~60-80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Ben Youssef Madrasa and Musée de Marrakech sell a combined ticket for ~100 MAD — ask at the entrance. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone souk walking. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) out of cultural respect.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD), a stunning 19th-century palace with intricate tilework and carved cedarwood ceilings. Then walk to the nearby El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD) — a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now hauntingly beautiful in its decay, with storks nesting on the ramparts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short taxi ride (~20 MAD) to the Majorelle Garden (entry ~150 MAD — worth every dirham), the cobalt-blue botanical garden made famous by Yves Saint Laurent. Also on-site is the Berber Museum (included in ticket). Afterwards, walk through the Gueliz neighbourhood (New City) for a change of pace and window shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Medina and visit a traditional hammam for an authentic Moroccan scrub experience. Budget hammams like Hammam Dar el-Bacha charge ~50-100 MAD for a basic session. Afterwards, enjoy dinner at a rooftop café overlooking Djemaa el-Fna.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast if included, or street-side café — café au lait and croissant (~15-20 MAD)
meals.lunch: Snack near Majorelle Garden — fresh fruit juice and a sandwich (~25-30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Rooftop café overlooking Djemaa el-Fna — pastilla or chicken tagine (~70-90 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam in the early afternoon to avoid evening rush. Majorelle Garden can be crowded — arrive right at opening (9:00 AM) or late afternoon. The Gueliz neighbourhood has ATMs if you need to withdraw more cash.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (6:00-7:00 AM) on a budget shared minibus/CTM bus or shared group tour heading toward Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi dunes. The journey takes approximately 9-10 hours via the Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass and the Draa Valley. Book through a budget tour agency in the Medina (shared group tours: ~400-600 MAD per person). Pack snacks and water for the road.
day_by_day.afternoon: En route stops typically include the Tizi n'Tichka Pass (2,260m elevation, stunning Atlas Mountain views), the ksar (fortified village) of Aït Benhaddou — a UNESCO World Heritage Site used in Game of Thrones and Gladiator (entry ~10 MAD, guide optional at ~50 MAD). Continue through Ouarzazate and the Draa Valley's palm groves.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Merzouga near the Erg Chebbi dunes around 17:00-18:00. Check in to a budget desert camp or guesthouse (~150-250 MAD per night). Mount a camel at sunset for a 45-60 minute ride into the dunes (often included in camp packages or ~100-150 MAD extra). Watch the sunset over the Sahara — one of the most breathtaking experiences in Morocco.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before departure — msemen and mint tea from a street vendor (~15 MAD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop at a local restaurant in Ouarzazate — tagine (~50-60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — harira, tagine, and Moroccan sweets (~included in camp or ~80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Sahara transport/tour at least 1-2 days in advance from agencies near Djemaa el-Fna. Compare prices from 2-3 agencies. Shared group tours are the most budget-friendly option. Bring a warm layer — desert nights in March can drop to 5-10°C. A headscarf/buff is useful against sand.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to climb the Erg Chebbi dunes on foot for a spectacular sunrise over the Sahara — absolutely free and unforgettable. The tallest dunes reach 150m. Return to camp for a Berber breakfast of bread, olive oil, honey, and mint tea. Explore the area around Merzouga village on foot or by rented bicycle (~50 MAD/day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a 4x4 excursion around the Erg Chebbi area (can be organised through your camp, ~150-200 MAD per person in a group). Visit the nomadic Berber families living near the dunes, the fossilised rock formations, and the small lake (Dayet Srji) that attracts flamingos in spring. Alternatively, sandboard down the dunes (boards rentable for ~50 MAD).
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp for the second sunset over the dunes. Enjoy a traditional Berber music session around a campfire — your camp hosts will play guembri and bendir drums under a sky full of stars (zero light pollution). This is one of the most magical evenings possible in Morocco.

meals.breakfast: Berber camp breakfast — bread, olive oil, honey, mint tea (included in most camps)
meals.lunch: Simple tagine or omelette at a local Merzouga café (~40-50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Camp dinner under the stars — Berber tagine, couscous, and sweet mint tea (included in camp or ~80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Protect your camera and phone from sand — use a zip-lock bag. Apply sunscreen generously; the desert sun in March is strong. Stay hydrated — carry at least 2 litres of water when exploring. Bargain politely for any additional activities offered by the camp.

day_by_day.date: 2027-03-20 (Return Journey: Sahara → Marrakech via Dades Gorge)
day_by_day.morning: Early morning camel ride back from the desert camp (if you stayed in the dunes overnight). Depart Merzouga around 7:00-8:00 AM for the return journey to Marrakech. The return route can include a stop at the dramatic Todra Gorge — towering 300m rock walls carved by a river, perfect for a short hike (free entry, ~1-2 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the stunning Dades Valley and Roses Valley (March is just before peak rose season, but the valley is still beautiful). Stop at the Dades Gorge for photos of the winding road and rock formations. Lunch stop in a small town like Boumalne Dades. Continue driving through the High Atlas toward Marrakech.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech around 19:00-20:00. Check back in to your Medina riad. Treat yourself to a sit-down dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant to celebrate the desert adventure — still budget-friendly. Relax with a final evening stroll through Djemaa el-Fna.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast before departure (included) or quick café stop in Merzouga (~20 MAD)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant in Boumalne Dades — tagine and bread (~50-60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Medina restaurant near your riad — couscous royale or pastilla (~80-100 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The return journey is long (9-10 hours with stops) — bring snacks, water, a book, and a music playlist. If your group tour is flexible, ask to stop at Todra Gorge — most drivers are happy to oblige. Confirm your riad reservation before departing the desert.

day_by_day.morning: Final Marrakech morning — visit the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) near the Bahia Palace for a quieter, less-touristy side of the Medina. Explore the covered market and the historic Jewish cemetery. Then head to the Spice Square (Rahba Kedima) to stock up on argan oil, ras el hanout spice mix, and dried rose petals as affordable gifts (~20-50 MAD each).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks — Moroccan leather slippers (babouches), hand-painted ceramics, and woven textiles make great budget gifts. Head to the tanneries (Souk des Teinturiers) for a final look from the viewing terraces above. Pack your bags back at the riad and arrange airport transport (petit taxi ~60-80 MAD or negotiate with your riad).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final sunset mint tea at a rooftop café overlooking the Medina. Have an early dinner before heading to the airport if your departure is in the evening, or a late dinner if flying the next morning. Reflect on an incredible week of culture, history, desert, and adventure in Morocco.

meals.breakfast: Final riad breakfast or classic Moroccan café — mint tea, msemen, amlou, and hard-boiled eggs (~25-30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Souk lunch — fresh-squeezed orange juice, kefta sandwich, and chebakia pastry (~25-30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a local Medina restaurant — mixed Moroccan mezze, tagine, and mint tea (~80-100 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Keep some MAD for the taxi to the airport and any last-minute purchases. Unused dirhams can be exchanged back at the airport (keep your exchange receipts). Budget summary for 7 days: accommodation ~700-1000 MAD, food ~1200-1500 MAD, transport ~800-1000 MAD, activities ~600-800 MAD, Sahara tour ~500-700 MAD — total approximately 3800-5000 MAD (~$380-500 USD) per person.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina district, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to boutique riad in the Medina near Djemaa el-Fna (~30 min by taxi, ~150 MAD). Check in, freshen up, and orient yourself with a short walk around the immediate neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle introduction to Djemaa el-Fna square: explore the open-air market stalls, watch street performers, snake charmers, and storytellers. Stroll into the northern edge of the souks (Souk Semmarine) to get a feel for the labyrinthine medina without going too deep on day one.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the iconic sunset transformation of Djemaa el-Fna as food stalls light up and the square fills with smoke and energy. Enjoy dinner at one of the open-air stalls on the square itself — try harira soup, kefta brochettes, and fresh-squeezed orange juice.

meals.breakfast: Skipped / light snack at airport before landing
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the riad after check-in — try a local café for a croque-monsieur or msemen (Moroccan flatbread) with honey and argan oil (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — stall No. 1 or stall 14 are popular; budget ~80–120 MAD for a full meal with fresh juice

day_by_day.notes: Keep valuables secure in the square — it gets very crowded at night. Ask your riad for a hand-drawn map of the immediate medina lanes. Exchange currency at a bank ATM rather than street exchanges.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior — non-Muslims cannot enter) for sunrise atmosphere and photos. Then head to the Saadian Tombs, a stunning 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917. Arrive before 9:30 to beat tour groups (~70 MAD entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Bahia Palace (Palace of the Vizier), a lavish 19th-century complex with ornate Moroccan tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and peaceful courtyards (~70 MAD entry). Afterward, wander the mellah (old Jewish quarter) nearby and browse antique shops.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Djemaa el-Fna for a rooftop café experience — Café de France or Café Argana offer great views over the square. Then dine at a proper Moroccan restaurant in the medina for a full tajine experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the riad (usually included) — expect msemen, baghrir (semolina pancakes), amlou (almond-argan dip), mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch near Bahia Palace — try Restaurant Foundouk or a local derb café; chicken tajine with preserved lemon ~80–120 MAD
meals.dinner: Restaurant Le Jardin in the medina (~150–200 MAD per person) — set in a beautiful courtyard garden; try lamb with prunes tajine and bastilla

day_by_day.notes: March weather in Marrakech is pleasant (~20–25°C) — light layers recommended for evenings. The Saadian Tombs open at 9:00; arrive early. Wear modest clothing when visiting historical/religious sites.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Atlas Mountains and Ouzoud Waterfalls (or Ourika Valley as an alternative). Depart by 8:00 via shared grand taxi or organized day-tour (~300–400 MAD per person). The Ouzoud Falls are Morocco's highest waterfalls at 110m, surrounded by olive groves and Barbary macaques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike down to the base of the falls, swim in the natural pools (March water is cool but refreshing), and take a short boat ride near the base (~20 MAD). Explore the Berber villages along the trail and interact with local families. Have lunch at one of the terrace restaurants overlooking the falls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Marrakech by 18:00–19:00. Relax at the riad, then explore the quieter streets of the medina at night — visit the spice market (Rahba Kedima square) for evening shopping.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the riad before 7:30 departure
meals.lunch: Terrace restaurant at Ouzoud Falls — fresh trout (farmed locally), salads, and Moroccan bread ~100–150 MAD with a drink
meals.dinner: Low-key dinner near the riad — try Snack Toubkal or a neighborhood restaurant for a simple chicken tagine or couscous ~70–100 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ouzoud excursion through your riad the night before for the best rate. Wear sturdy shoes for the waterfall hike. Bring a swimsuit if you plan to swim. The drive is about 2.5 hours each way through scenic Berber countryside.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (~7:00) for the Sahara Desert via the spectacular Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m). This is a long driving day (~9–10 hours total) — book a private driver or join a shared desert tour (~600–800 MAD per person for a 2-day desert package). Stop at the dramatic Aït Benhaddou ksar (UNESCO World Heritage Site) — a fortified Berber village used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley and Dadès Gorges region toward Merzouga. The landscape transforms dramatically from mountains to desert steppes to dunes. Stop at a roadside argan cooperative for a demonstration and purchase if desired.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Merzouga (gateway to Erg Chebbi dunes) around 17:00–18:00. Mount camels for a 1-hour sunset trek into the Sahara dunes. Arrive at a mid-range desert camp with private Berber tents, shared bathroom facilities, and a communal fire pit.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at riad before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch stop in Ouarzazate or near Aït Benhaddou — Restaurant Chez Dimitri or a local café; Moroccan salads, tagine ~100–130 MAD
meals.dinner: Dinner at the desert camp (usually included in camp package) — traditional Berber meal with harira, tagine, couscous, and mint tea under the stars

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day — bring water, snacks, sunscreen, and a good playlist. The Tizi n'Tichka pass can have traffic; depart no later than 7:00. Aït Benhaddou entry ~10 MAD. Desert camp should be pre-booked — look for camps with private tents and good reviews (~400–600 MAD per person including dinner, breakfast, and camel ride).

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (~5:30) to climb the Erg Chebbi dunes for a breathtaking Sahara sunrise — one of Morocco's most iconic experiences. The silence, the color gradients of sand, and the vast emptiness are extraordinary. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional activities near Merzouga: quad biking on the dunes (~250–350 MAD/hour), visit to a Gnawa music village, or a 4x4 desert excursion to fossil sites and nomadic camps. Alternatively, relax at the camp, read, and absorb the silence of the desert.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return journey toward Marrakech, stopping overnight in Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') — check into a mid-range hotel like Hotel Dar Kamar or Riad Salam (~400–600 MAD/night). Evening walk through Ouarzazate's kasbah district.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at desert camp (included) — Berber bread, olive oil, honey, amlou, mint tea
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch en route — stop in Boumalne Dadès or Skoura for a simple tagine at a local auberge ~80–100 MAD
meals.dinner: Dinner in Ouarzazate — Restaurant Chez Talout or hotel restaurant; try mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) or pastilla au poulet ~150–180 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Bring a headlamp for the pre-dawn dune climb. Sand can be cold at night and early morning in March (~8–12°C) — pack a warm layer. Sandstorms are rare in March but carry a scarf/shemagh to protect your face just in case.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Taourirt Kasbah in Ouarzazate — a magnificent 19th-century earthen fortress and UNESCO-listed site (~20 MAD entry). Then visit the Atlas Film Studios — the world's largest film studios where Lawrence of Arabia, The Mummy, and many others were filmed (~80 MAD entry, fascinating behind-the-scenes sets).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back to Marrakech via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (~3.5 hours). Arrive in Marrakech by mid-afternoon. Check back into your riad and refresh. Spend the late afternoon doing serious souk shopping — Souk des Teinturiers (dyers' souk), Souk Cherratine (leather), and Souk Haddadine (metalworkers).
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a farewell-eve dinner at one of Marrakech's celebrated mid-range restaurants. Enjoy live Gnawa or Andalusian music if available at your chosen venue.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Ouarzazate hotel before 8:00 departure
meals.lunch: Picnic or roadside café stop in the Atlas Mountains — packed sandwiches from a local boulangerie in Ouarzazate ~30–50 MAD, or stop at a mountain auberge
meals.dinner: Nomad Restaurant in the Medina (~180–250 MAD per person) — modern Moroccan cuisine on a rooftop with views of the souks; try the lamb mechoui and date crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: Haggling is expected in the souks — start at 40–50% of the asking price and meet in the middle. Leather goods, spices, argan oil, and handwoven rugs are excellent buys. Keep receipts for customs if buying ceramics or antiques.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the Majorelle Garden (formerly owned by Yves Saint Laurent), a stunning botanical garden with cobalt-blue buildings, exotic cacti, and tranquil pools (~150 MAD entry; arrive at 8:00 when it opens to avoid crowds). The adjacent Berber Museum within the garden is excellent (~30 MAD extra).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping or café time in Gueliz (the French-built new town) — more relaxed than the medina with fixed-price boutiques. Visit the YSL Museum if interested in fashion and art (~100 MAD). Head back to the riad, collect luggage, and transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech — allow 2 hours before your flight. Enjoy one final mint tea at the airport or a nearby café before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Final riad breakfast — savor the mint tea, msemen, and fresh fruit one last time
meals.lunch: Lunch in Gueliz at Café du Livre or Grand Café de la Poste — French-Moroccan fusion in a colonial setting ~120–160 MAD
meals.dinner: Light meal or snack at the airport, or grab a quick bite from a medina café before the transfer if time allows

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden gets very crowded after 10:00 — the 8:00 opening slot is ideal. Taxi to the airport from the medina takes 15–20 minutes and costs ~100–150 MAD (agree on price before getting in). Keep 100–200 MAD in cash for tips and last-minute purchases. Morocco requires passports valid for 6+ months beyond travel dates.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina district, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to your boutique riad in the Medina district near Djemaa el-Fna. Settle in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome mint tea ceremony hosted by your riad staff.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation stroll through Djemaa el-Fna square and the surrounding souks — experience the sensory explosion of spice merchants, artisan stalls, and street performers. Visit the iconic Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior) just a short walk from the riad. Optional: private guided introduction to the Medina's layout with a personal cultural guide arranged through the riad concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset rooftop aperitif at your riad's terrace overlooking the Medina skyline and the illuminated Koutoubia minaret. Immerse in the electric atmosphere of Djemaa el-Fna as dusk transforms the square into an open-air theatre of storytellers, musicians, and food vendors.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (mid-day arrival)
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the riad or a light meal at Café de France terrace overlooking Djemaa el-Fna — traditional harira soup, msemen flatbread, and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Foundouk — a celebrated upscale Moroccan-French fusion restaurant in the Medina, set inside a beautifully restored 18th-century caravanserai. Try the bastilla au pigeon and slow-braised lamb with preserved lemon. Reservation essential.

day_by_day.notes: Flight code noted as LH — confirm private airport transfer in advance. Ask the riad concierge to brief you on the 7-day itinerary and pre-book all experiences and restaurants this evening to secure availability.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Bahia Palace — a breathtaking 19th-century royal palace with ornate zellij tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush Andalusian gardens. Follow with a visit to the Saadian Tombs, the opulent mausoleum of the Saadian dynasty, featuring Italian Carrara marble and intricate stucco work. Both sites are within walking distance or a short carriage ride from the Medina.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and its historic synagogues with a private historian guide. Visit the Maison de la Photographie for a stunning rooftop view and curated collection of early 20th-century Moroccan photography. End the afternoon with a private artisan workshop experience — learn traditional zellige mosaic or leather tanning craft with a master craftsman.
day_by_day.evening: Private hammam and spa ritual at a luxury hammam such as Hammam de la Rose or Les Bains de Marrakech — enjoy a traditional black soap scrub, ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage. Return refreshed for a leisurely evening in the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Elaborate Moroccan breakfast at the riad — msemen, beghrir (semolina crepes), amlou (argan & almond spread), fresh fruit, honey, and spiced coffee or mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad — a chic rooftop restaurant in the souks with contemporary Moroccan cuisine. Try the lamb kefta briouats and the vegetable couscous with seven vegetables
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Maison Arabe — one of Marrakech's most prestigious dining institutions. Enjoy a multi-course Moroccan tasting menu featuring pastilla, tangia, and seasonal desserts in an elegant riad setting with live Gnawa music

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the hammam session (2–3 hours recommended). Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina. Hire a licensed private guide for the historical sites to gain deeper cultural context.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Atlas Mountains — private luxury 4x4 transfer through the Tizi n'Tichka pass. Morning stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou ksar (fortified village), one of Morocco's most spectacular earthen architecture sites and a famous film location (Gladiator, Game of Thrones). Private guided walk through the ancient ksar with a local Berber historian.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Draa Valley or nearby Berber villages for a traditional lunch. Optional camel ride or mule trek through the surrounding palmery. Visit a local argan oil cooperative run by Berber women — learn about the ancient harvest process and purchase premium cold-pressed argan oil directly from the source.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to Marrakech by sunset (approximately 2.5-hour drive). Relax at the riad with a private rooftop dinner or head out for a quiet evening in the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Early Moroccan breakfast at the riad before departure
meals.lunch: Traditional Berber lunch at a family-run restaurant in Aït Benhaddou or the Draa Valley — slow-cooked lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, fresh bread from a clay oven, and Berber whisky (mint tea)
meals.dinner: Intimate rooftop dinner at the riad arranged by your concierge — private chef prepares a curated Moroccan menu with local seasonal ingredients, candlelit under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Depart early (7:30 AM) to arrive at Aït Benhaddou before tour groups. Bring sun protection, a light jacket for the mountain altitude, and comfortable shoes for uneven terrain. This is a long day — approximately 10–12 hours total.

day_by_day.morning: Departure from Marrakech by private luxury 4x4 for the Sahara Desert — the classic route via Ouarzazate, the Draa Valley, and Zagora or the longer route to Merzouga (Erg Chebbi dunes). Scenic drive through dramatic gorges, kasbahs, and oasis towns. Stop at the Fint Oasis near Ouarzazate for a peaceful walk through palm groves and a traditional kasbah visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue toward the Sahara. Stop at Erfoud or Rissani for a brief exploration of the fossil-rich region and local date market. As the landscape shifts to golden sand, arrive at the edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga in the late afternoon. Check in to a luxury desert camp — expect private en-suite tented suites with plush furnishings, solar lighting, and panoramic dune views.
day_by_day.evening: Camel trek into the heart of the Sahara dunes at golden hour — ride to a prime dune crest to watch the sunset paint the sand in shades of amber and crimson. Stargazing session with a private astronomer or camp guide using high-powered telescopes in one of the world's darkest skies. Traditional Berber music and drumming around a campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the riad before departure
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch at a curated restaurant in Ouarzazate or a luxury stop at the Berbère Palace Hotel — lamb couscous and fresh salads
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner under the stars at the luxury desert camp — traditional Moroccan feast including harira, mechoui (slow-roasted lamb), couscous, and Moroccan pastries. Non-alcoholic beverages and premium still water served

day_by_day.notes: The Marrakech-to-Merzouga drive is approximately 8–9 hours — consider a scenic overnight stop in Ouarzazate on the way if preferred (adjust itinerary accordingly). Pack warm layers — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Confirm luxury camp booking well in advance as top-tier camps have limited tented suites.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a sunrise camel or 4x4 dune ride to the highest dune crest — watch the Sahara awaken in extraordinary light. Optional sandboarding on the dunes. Return to camp for a leisurely breakfast. Explore the local Berber village of Merzouga on foot or by 4x4 — visit a nomadic family, learn about desert survival traditions, and observe the unique blue-dye indigo textile craft of the Tuareg people.
day_by_day.afternoon: Quad biking or private 4x4 desert excursion across the erg — discover hidden oases, fossil beds, and remote nomadic encampments. Visit the Gnawa musicians' community in Khamlia village for a private traditional music performance — an extraordinary cultural experience. Afternoon relaxation at the camp with a Berber herbal tea ritual and optional massage treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Second night at the luxury desert camp. Private sunset photography session on the dunes with a professional guide. Elaborate Berber dinner celebration at the camp with live music, traditional storytelling, and a bonfire. Opportunity for a solo midnight dune walk under an extraordinary canopy of stars.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at the camp after sunrise — fresh bread, eggs, honey, argan oil, seasonal fruits, and spiced coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the camp or a picnic prepared by camp staff during the desert excursion — Moroccan sandwiches, olives, dates, and fresh juice
meals.dinner: Grand Berber feast at the camp — multiple courses including spiced lamb mechoui, vegetable tagine, mint tea ceremony, and traditional sweets. Served on low cushioned seating around the campfire

day_by_day.notes: Protect cameras and electronics from fine desert sand using sealed bags. Sunrise is approximately 7:00 AM in mid-March. The Khamlia village visit is a highlight — tip the musicians generously. Hydration is critical in the desert — drink at least 2–3 liters of water throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise moment at the dunes before departure. Private 4x4 transfer back toward Marrakech via the scenic northern route through the Ziz Valley, Midelt, and the Middle Atlas — a dramatically different landscape of cedar forests, Berber market towns, and snow-dusted mountain peaks. Stop at the cedar forest near Azrou to spot wild Barbary macaques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the journey through Ifrane — Morocco's 'Little Switzerland' — a charming alpine town with European-style architecture and manicured parks. Optional stop for a coffee break. Arrive back in Marrakech in the late afternoon. Check back into your riad and decompress with a relaxing bath, hammam, or spa treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell evening in Marrakech — final exploration of the Djemaa el-Fna at night, soaking in the atmosphere of fire dancers, snake charmers, and open-air food stalls. Optional private calèche (horse-drawn carriage) ride around the ramparts of the Medina at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the desert camp before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch stop in Midelt or Ifrane — try a local mountain restaurant specializing in trout from the Atlas rivers, fresh salads, and Berber bread
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner at Dar Yacout — Marrakech's most theatrical fine dining experience, set in a stunning palace riad with rooftop cocktails, live music, and an elaborate Moroccan tasting menu. Dress elegantly. Reservation essential and highly sought-after.

day_by_day.notes: The return route via the Middle Atlas adds approximately 1–2 hours but is significantly more scenic and culturally rich than retracing the Ouarzazate road. Confirm riad check-in time in advance. Use the evening to purchase last-minute artisan gifts from the souks — argan oil, saffron, handwoven leather goods, and Moroccan ceramics.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — leisurely breakfast at the riad. Last-minute souk shopping for premium Moroccan crafts: visit the Ensemble Artisanal (government-regulated fixed-price artisan center) for quality-assured purchases. Explore the Majorelle Garden and Villa Oasis — the iconic cobalt-blue botanical garden created by painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent, with the adjacent Musée Berbère housing an extraordinary collection of Amazigh artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Yves Saint Laurent Museum adjacent to Majorelle Garden — a world-class modern museum celebrating the designer's deep love affair with Morocco, featuring rotating exhibitions of haute couture and Moroccan-inspired collections. Enjoy a final mint tea at the garden café. Private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech — carry the magic of Morocco home. Ensure all premium purchases are properly packed (argan oil in checked luggage, fragile ceramics bubble-wrapped).

meals.breakfast: Final elaborate Moroccan breakfast at the riad — a leisurely send-off with all traditional favorites: msemen, amlou, fresh fruit, honey, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Majorelle Garden café or a final meal at Grand Café de la Poste — a colonial-era brasserie with elegant Moroccan-French cuisine, perfect for a refined farewell lunch
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining (departure dependent on flight time)

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden is extremely popular — arrive at opening time (9:00 AM) to avoid crowds. The YSL Museum requires a separate ticket from the garden. Allow at least 3 hours at the airport for international departure. Keep all receipts for luxury goods for customs declarations. Consider tipping riad staff generously as a farewell gesture — 200–300 MAD per staff member is appropriate for a 7-day luxury stay.
